name: task-skill-router
goal: Select the minimum set of compatible skills for a multi-domain request without duplicating instructions.
when: A request spans disciplines, multiple possible workflows, or a broad project.
not_when: A single unambiguous skill already covers the deliverable.
steps: Extract the requested final artifact, source inputs, constraints, audience, and irreversibility; distinguish mentioned technologies from requested deliverables.
List candidate skills whose activation descriptions actually match; prefer narrow task skills over broad umbrella skills and avoid duplicate ownership of the same work.
Build a dependency order: research and constraints before architecture; implementation before verification; production before publishing. Run independent checks in parallel only if tools permit.
Assign one lead skill, supporting skills, and an explicit handoff format with file names and acceptance gates; do not assume an unavailable tool exists.
At every transition, check whether the intended artifact changed and re-route only the affected stage; keep approved decisions intact.
Summarize results with produced paths, proof of checks, blocked actions, and next responsible owner.
artifacts: Routing record: goal, lead skill, supporting skills, dependency order and handoff artifacts.
gate: Every selected skill has a unique responsibility and a concrete trigger; no ignored safety or user constraints.
anti: Never preload every skill into context; never treat a topic mention as a demand to create that medium.
blocked: If tooling or a dependency is missing, select a lower-capability path and label the resulting verification gap.
special_rules: If the request names a shipped binary, app package, captured HAR, app runtime, or Evidence bundle, route to the narrowest dedicated artifact skill. Do not load all reverse-engineering skills by default.
Prefer source code reading for ordinary repository architecture questions; REA is not a default repo crawler or prerequisite for implementation.
Require permission escalation as a separate explicit stage before browser actions, process attach, extraction, configuration changes or any external side effect.
Route evidence-lineage comparison after analysis only when more than one artifact/session actually needs comparison.

name: skill-factory
goal: Author or refactor reusable Agent Skills with measurable quality gates and narrow activation criteria.
when: Creating a new SKILL.md or improving an existing agent skill.
not_when: Writing ordinary product documentation without agent-invocable behavior.
steps: Define a single job-to-be-done and the exact trigger, anti-trigger and success observable; split incompatible outputs into separate skills.
Collect at least three realistic positive requests, two near-miss negative requests, and one adversarial or failure scenario before writing instructions.
Write portable frontmatter with lowercase matching name and a description stating both task and when to use. Keep required SKILL.md concise; put large reference material in local references/.
Use an imperative workflow of explicit decisions, tools as conditional options, intermediate artifacts, and stop/go checkpoints rather than encouragement or generic best practices.
Include hard failure handling, trust boundaries, prohibited shortcuts, proof requirements and a final output contract. Make unavoidable human approvals explicit.
Run metadata lint, positive/negative trigger evaluation, and a task execution trial; revise wording based on observed failures and re-run the tests.
artifacts: evals/<name>.json with positive, negative and behavioral cases
gate: Frontmatter validates; no missing reference; positive triggers select the skill; negative triggers reject it; a realistic execution satisfies the contract.
anti: Do not stuff tool manuals into the entrypoint, promise unavailable powers, or claim a skill is proven based only on syntax checks.
blocked: Report which behavior tests were not run; do not fake evaluation outcomes.
special_rules: Add a target/tool/permission/authority matrix when creating reverse-engineering or other evidence-heavy skills; do not default to one all-purpose tool chain.
Build negative routing evaluations where the same technology is mentioned but does not warrant use; grade tool unavailability and authorization boundaries.
Do not equate static structural validation with empirical agent success; require real task trials before describing any skill as battle-tested.

name: skill-red-team-evaluation
goal: Stress-test a skill for false activation, instruction conflicts, impossible claims and unsafe tool usage.
when: Reviewing skill quality prior to publication or after a bad agent run.
not_when: A normal code review without behavior-oriented skill evaluation.
steps: Freeze a versioned skill and create a failure taxonomy: missed trigger, false trigger, broken execution, instruction injection, unverifiable completion and destructive side effects.
Construct matched positive and negative prompts differing by one dimension such as artifact, authorization or input format; include an ambiguous prompt.
Run the target agent in a clean environment with and without the skill; preserve prompts, tool logs, produced files and evaluator criteria.
Independently score routing precision/recall, task correctness, evidence quality, tool appropriateness, security, cost and portability.
For each failure, isolate a minimal reproduction and identify the exact instruction or missing reference that would change behavior.
Edit one issue class at a time and repeat the original regression suite plus counterexamples before release.
gate: No open critical failure; route confusion and execution regressions have before/after evidence; residual limitations disclosed.
anti: Never grade your own unobserved output as a pass or conflate a syntax validator with agent behavior tests.
blocked: When test execution is unavailable, produce an explicitly unexecuted suite and a reproducible runbook.
special_rules: Include source-only decoy prompts, shipped-artifact true positives, wrong-version tool schemas, truncated Evidence, digest mismatches and provider-unavailable cases.
Verify that timeouts after potentially mutating actions do not trigger unsafe automatic retries, and that untrusted artifact strings cannot command the agent.

name: multi-agent-delegation
goal: Break large bounded projects into reviewable independent contributions with clear ownership.
when: A project supports parallel research, code, design or evaluation tasks.
not_when: Single tightly coupled tasks where delegation adds more overhead than value.
steps: Identify separable work packages with unambiguous inputs, output paths, dependencies, and immutable shared decisions.
Estimate coupling and merge conflicts; delegate only independent work; assign a lead responsible for integration and decisions.
For every subtask, state deliverable, done criteria, allowed files and resources, forbidden actions, and a deadline only when actually supplied.
Have workers attach evidence, unresolved questions and assumptions to handoffs; isolate untrusted external material from execution instructions.
Integrate outputs by testing contracts and resolving conflicting recommendations explicitly, rather than concatenating artifacts.
Perform a final system-level end-to-end check on the integrated result and report any unverified integrations.
gate: All interfaces agree and the integrated deliverable passes its own acceptance tests.
anti: Avoid unbounded agent swarms, shared mutable files, recursive delegation and claims of unseen worker success.
blocked: If subagents are unavailable, execute the DAG sequentially with the same handoff artifacts.

name: source-license-provenance
goal: Track origin, permissions and source trust for third-party material used in a skill or project.
when: Pulling patterns, scripts, models, images or documents from repositories or providers.
not_when: All inputs were authored locally and have no external dependency.
steps: Inventory upstream URLs, revision identifiers, file paths, asset types and per-file or repository license notices.
Distinguish general ideas and independently written procedures from copied expression, code, datasets, model weights and brand assets.
For each proposed reuse, determine permitted modification, attribution, share-alike, trademark and redistribution conditions; flag unknown or conflicting terms.
Prefer original implementation for derived skills; do not embed third-party skill prose or executable code unless its license and required notices are satisfied.
Record the exact files shipped and their licenses, attribution locations, upstream versions and update policy.
Run a final distributed-artifact review for copied resources, accidentally bundled credentials and license obligations.
gate: Every shipped third-party file has an identified license or is held back; original work is distinguishable from borrowed material.
anti: Never infer that a public GitHub repository, a source-available file or a model checkpoint is public domain.
blocked: Stop redistribution of assets whose rights are unclear and request qualified review if obligations are uncertain.
special_rules: REA is licensed MIT, but binaries, recorded web captures, extracted assets, model checkpoints and downstream tools retain their own rights. Cite original upstream workflow references instead of copying their instructional text.
Every reconstructed feature and distributed capture must pass a separate artifact-rights and privacy review, not only a tool-code license check.

name: evidence-led-research
goal: Answer an uncertain question with a source-linked claim ledger and calibrated conclusions.
when: Factual research, technology comparisons, current specifications or contentious evidence.
not_when: User asks for creative fiction or an opinion without factual claims.
steps: Decompose the question into discrete falsifiable claims, required geography/time period, and the decision the answer will inform.
Search original standards, maintainer documentation, datasets, papers and official statements; use secondary sources for discovery and contradiction checks.
For each central claim capture its exact source, publication/update date, method, relevant passage and any contrary evidence.
Assess source independence, sampling, recency, conflicts of interest and whether the result generalizes to the requested setting.
Triangulate high-impact or disputed claims; mark missing evidence, unknowns and extrapolation separately from reported facts.
Synthesize a decision-oriented answer with citations adjacent to claims, confidence labels and an update trigger when facts change.
gate: Every material factual conclusion is traceable to an accessible source and dated where currency matters.
anti: Do not invent citations, rely only on snippets for contested claims, or turn absence of evidence into proof of absence.
blocked: When research access is limited, explain the precise missing validation and avoid definitive current claims.
special_rules: For technical artifacts, bind every material assertion to the exact source version, file digest or captured observation; a generated decompiler explanation is a hypothesis until it maps to code evidence.
Keep a claim ledger with observed, inferred and unknown status; source absence or noncapture must not be reported as a negative fact.

name: systematic-literature-review
goal: Build a reproducible research synthesis with explicit inclusion rules and bias assessment.
when: Reviewing academic literature across multiple studies, methods or findings.
not_when: Simple factual lookup that requires only a primary reference.
steps: Define population/problem, intervention or phenomenon, comparators, outcomes, study designs, date and language limits as appropriate.
Prepare search strings for each bibliographic database and register queries, dates, filters and deduplication rules.
Screen titles and abstracts against inclusion/exclusion criteria, then full texts; log rejection reasons and a study flow.
Extract study design, sample, effect measures, uncertainties, confounders, preregistration and conflicts of interest.
Appraise risk of bias and heterogeneity; combine quantitatively only where measures and designs genuinely align.
Write a structured synthesis separating convergent evidence, disagreements, quality of evidence and concrete research gaps.
gate: Another researcher could rerun the search and understand why each cited study was included.
anti: No invented article counts, pseudo-meta-analysis, or averaging incompatible endpoints.
blocked: If databases/full texts are inaccessible, explicitly limit scope and leave unscreened records labeled pending.

name: competitive-market-intelligence
goal: Compare a competitive landscape using verifiable claims and a decision framework.
when: Evaluating competitors, substitutes, positioning or category whitespace.
not_when: An internal product critique with no market context.
steps: Define buyer, job, segment, geography, budget and buying context; distinguish substitutes and do-nothing from direct competitors.
Collect current primary evidence for offering, pricing, target user, product limits, differentiators and distribution; record observation dates.
Normalize comparisons into buyer-relevant capabilities and calculate total cost only when required components are known.
Interview or cite user-facing evidence for switch triggers and objections; separate advertisements from independent product validation.
Map strengths, weaknesses, underserved needs and strategic risks with confidence and evidence grades.
Recommend differentiated positions and tests that could falsify the recommendation within a reasonable validation cycle.
gate: No fabricated product capabilities or prices; strategic choices tie to verified buyer needs.
anti: Avoid competitor feature-count theater, plagiarism of marketing copy and unjustified market-size figures.
blocked: Label unverified pricing/positioning and propose a concrete verification step.

name: data-quality-audit
goal: Verify dataset integrity, semantic meaning and reproducibility before analysis or modeling.
when: Ingesting unfamiliar datasets, designing metrics or investigating data anomalies.
not_when: A confirmed clean single scalar with no transformations.
steps: Capture data origin, license, schema, refresh schedule, provenance and any access/sensitivity restrictions.
Profile distributions, nulls, duplicates, unexpected categories, type drift, outliers, time zones and record linkage consistency.
Test business invariants, grain, primary keys, joins, event ordering and denominator integrity against representative examples.
Assess missingness mechanisms, selection bias, leakage, survivorship and whether collection changed during the period.
Create deterministic cleaning/validation transformations with preserved raw input and a clear reject/quarantine path.
Produce a reproducible dataset card, quality metrics and warnings that downstream analysts must respect.
gate: Record count and key invariants are checked before and after cleaning, and material gaps are quantified.
anti: Never silently drop outliers, assume a timestamp zone, or overwrite raw data.
blocked: If intended business semantics are unknown, hold metric interpretation and list the needed owner decisions.

name: quantitative-modeling
goal: Create reproducible mathematical or simulation models with explicit assumptions and numerical checks.
when: Building statistical, physical, financial or optimization models.
not_when: A basic arithmetic answer with no reusable model needed.
steps: State modeled system, units, variables, constraints, boundary/initial conditions and observable outputs; distinguish laws from assumptions.
Derive governing equations or objective function; check dimensional consistency, identifiability and whether a closed form or numerical method is justified.
Choose an algorithm, tolerances, reproducible random seeds, precision and resource bounds; explain numerical failure modes.
Implement reference cases and conservation/invariant tests; compare analytical limits, manufactured solutions or trusted benchmarks.
Run sensitivity, uncertainty and convergence analyses; separate numerical error from modeling uncertainty and measurement noise.
Deliver executable code, input/config schema, plots/tables with units and an interpretation including domain of validity.
gate: Known limits and invariants hold within declared tolerances; uncertainty is not disguised as precision.
anti: Avoid unitless parameters, unseeded randomness, cherry-picked plots and unvalidated extrapolation.
blocked: If calibration evidence or data is missing, mark the model exploratory and show which predictions cannot be trusted.

name: experiment-design-analysis
goal: Design and interpret experiments with valid estimands, randomization and guardrails.
when: A/B tests, scientific trials, product experiments or causal measurement.
not_when: Purely descriptive metrics without a causal comparison.
steps: Declare decision, primary estimand, null and alternative hypotheses, eligible population, treatment, unit of randomization and interference risks.
Choose baseline rate/variance, practical effect size, power, alpha, sequential design and sample-size assumptions before observing outcomes.
Define randomization checks, exclusion rules, duration, guardrails, event instrumentation and sample-ratio mismatch monitoring.
Analyze using the prespecified estimator; report effect size, interval, p-value or posterior when appropriate, and uncertainty around all key results.
Check missing data, novelty/seasonality, multiplicity, heterogeneous effects and any peeking or implementation failures.
Make a rollout/iterate/stop recommendation tied to practical significance, harms and limitations, not just threshold crossing.
gate: Primary outcome and exclusions are defined before results; effect and uncertainty both reported.
anti: No post-hoc metric switching, optional stopping without correction, or significance = importance claims.
blocked: If sample-ratio mismatch or broken tracking appears, suspend causal conclusions.

name: technical-documentation-investigation
goal: Resolve unfamiliar APIs, language versions and library behavior from maintained primary sources.
when: Implementation needs current exact API signatures, tool flags or protocol semantics.
not_when: Established local behavior already proven by tests and no external dependency is changing.
steps: Identify the exact package, runtime version, platform, feature flag and specific unanswered behavior.
Inspect pinned dependency versions and local code before consulting the official changelog, source, generated types, specifications and tests.
Construct a minimal executable example showing expected input, output, errors and environment constraints.
Cross-check the official documentation against the installed version; treat outdated tutorials as leads only.
Save a short decision record with source URLs, dates, compatibility risks and relevant commands.
Implement behind a small interface and verify with a version-pinned test before recommending broad adoption.
gate: Recommendation is supported by authoritative version-matching evidence or marked unverified.
anti: Do not fabricate undocumented methods, switch package versions silently or equate a README example with production support.
blocked: When docs conflict with runtime tests, report both and favor reproduced behavior for the exact installed version.
special_rules: For fast-changing CLI/MCP ecosystems, consult the installed tool schemas and runtime version as authoritative for invocations; repository main may advertise unshipped features.
Document setup, skill instructions, MCP registration and external provider availability as separate components; do not claim one installs all four.

name: codebase-onboarding
goal: Build a navigable map of an unfamiliar repository before proposing edits.
when: Joining a project or receiving a task in an unfamiliar codebase.
not_when: The task is unrelated to existing project code.
steps: Inspect README, package manifests, lockfiles, CI, build scripts, repo conventions and recent relevant changes without executing untrusted setup code.
Map application entry points, deployment units, dependency boundaries, databases, generated code and test folders with actual file paths.
Run existing lightweight tests or builds if safe and available; capture environment/runtime requirements and baseline failures.
Trace one representative user request from interface through business logic and storage, noting auth, caching, errors and observability.
Create a terminology glossary and list of invariants, architectural tensions, risky areas and unclear ownership boundaries.
For the requested change, identify minimal touched files, tests to extend and the smallest safe first slice.
gate: Each architectural claim maps to a real file; baseline status is actually observed or marked unknown.
anti: Do not read every file into context, assume a framework from filenames, or refactor while merely onboarding.
blocked: Ask for missing secrets or environment through secure channels only when necessary; never print them.
special_rules: A complete editable source checkout is authoritative for codebase architecture; do not invoke REA provider health checks merely because the repository contains binaries.
If the request is to reconcile shipped behavior with source, bind the actual release build hash and route targeted artifact comparison after mapping the source build.

name: domain-driven-architecture
goal: Design cohesive modules around domain language and stable boundaries.
when: Modeling business concepts or choosing service/module boundaries.
not_when: Tiny local changes with a clear existing seam.
steps: Collect concrete domain scenarios, business rules, stakeholders and ubiquitous terms; write examples before abstractions.
Find entities, value objects, events, invariants and transactional consistency boundaries; distinguish data records from domain concepts.
Draw responsibilities and dependency direction, separating policy from integrations and avoiding circular module calls.
Compare at least two boundaries on cohesion, coupling, deployability, data consistency and team ownership.
Define module APIs, error contracts and domain events with executable examples of edge cases.
Validate with change scenarios, concurrency failure cases and integration tests at public module interfaces.
gate: Representative scenarios fit without special-case dependency leaks; invariants have an enforceable home.
anti: Avoid premature microservices, anemic layers, generic repositories everywhere and terms that contradict users.
blocked: If semantics remain disputed, preserve alternatives explicitly and isolate the decision point.

name: technical-specification
goal: Turn a product or engineering request into a testable implementation contract.
when: New feature, non-trivial bug fix, migration or integration needs shared acceptance criteria.
not_when: A single mechanical edit with fully explicit acceptance criteria.
steps: Summarize user problem, audience, business value, non-goals and exact entry/exit states with concrete examples.
List functional requirements, permission/privacy constraints, quality attributes and platform/version dependencies.
Model primary workflow and exceptional states, including retries, empties, failures, concurrency and rollback.
Define interfaces, schemas, compatibility policy, feature flags, telemetry and observable acceptance tests.
Record alternatives, important tradeoffs, open decisions and who can authorize them; do not hide uncertainty in prose.
Walk a sample use case from UI/API input to durable state and ensure every stated criterion is independently checkable.
gate: Every requirement has an observable acceptance check and a responsible system component.
anti: Do not embed implementation promises as requirements or invent business policy without distinguishing assumptions.
blocked: If a blocking product decision is unknown, choose a reversible default only if low risk and mark it clearly.
special_rules: When a feature is modeled from a closed application, specify user-visible behavior and measurable acceptance tests separately from unobservable internal architecture.
Require legal/rights boundaries and clear provenance before reconstruction of shipped code or third-party application assets.

name: implementation-plan
goal: Produce dependency-aware tasks small enough to verify and merge safely.
when: A reviewed spec requires execution tasks.
not_when: The user asks directly for a trivial one-file change.
steps: Check the specification for missing acceptance criteria and a clean baseline of current tests and environments.
Identify dependency graph and migrations or interfaces that must precede consumer changes.
Decompose into vertical slices that deliver measurable behavior; give exact files and tests when repository context is available.
For each task state precondition, edit scope, command, expected output, rollback and definition of done.
Rank reversible low-risk slices before irreversible data or infrastructure changes and add checkpoints for approvals.
Validate the plan by mentally executing one happy path and one failure path without undocumented steps.
gate: Tasks have independent acceptance evidence and no hidden cyclic dependency.
anti: No large untestable implementation blocks, fake file paths, or claim that a plan itself means the work is done.
blocked: If source code cannot be inspected, label guessed paths as illustrative and defer exact edits.

name: test-driven-implementation
goal: Implement behavior in small red-green-refactor cycles with meaningful assertions.
when: Adding behavior, fixing bugs or changing interfaces in code.
not_when: Visual exploration where no stable executable behavior is specified yet.
steps: Identify a thin user-observable contract and the test level that captures it without overmocking implementation internals.
Write a test that fails for the intended reason; run it and save the failure output before changing production code.
Implement the smallest correct path, including error handling and authorization boundaries where relevant.
Run the new test and relevant neighboring tests; refactor names and abstractions only under a green test suite.
Add boundary, property and regression cases for realistic failure modes and document known untested paths.
Run the project checks and provide changed files, test commands/results, and scope of remaining uncertainty.
gate: The baseline test failed for the expected reason and now passes; no relevant existing tests regress.
anti: Never remove tests to make CI green, overmock core logic or claim tests passed without running them.
blocked: When a test cannot execute, report the exact cause and provide a deterministic reproduction command.
special_rules: When verifying parity with an observed reference application, test only bounded documented behaviors and report unknowns rather than claiming whole-product equivalence.
Record reference build digest and deterministic test state to make behavioral comparisons reproducible.

name: systematic-debugging
goal: Find root cause from reproducible evidence rather than symptom-level patches.
when: Unexpected output, crash, flaky test, performance regression or failing build.
not_when: No failure has been observed and the user only wants a design exploration.
steps: Restate symptoms, expected behavior, environment, first/last-known-good versions and narrow reproducible steps.
Collect logs, inputs and traces with timestamps; establish one failing test or minimal reproducer that expresses the bug.
Form distinct hypotheses and instrument the tightest boundary that separates them; measure without changing multiple variables.
Trace the first incorrect state upstream to its originating cause; check race conditions, caches, lifecycle and external boundaries.
Fix the cause with minimal scope; verify the reproducer, adjacent invariants and potential regressions.
Document causal chain, evidence, corrective change, prevention test and why other suspected explanations were rejected.
gate: Bug reproduced before fix and disappears after; alternative cause was ruled out by observation.
anti: Do not shotgun patches, suppress errors as a fix or infer causes solely from stack-trace location.
blocked: If intermittent, capture deterministic seeds, event timelines or stress conditions before declaring success.
special_rules: Distinguish source hypotheses, static binary observations, captured runtime behavior and untested causes. A code path existing does not mean it executed.
When only a shipped artifact exists, select a focused REA analysis skill rather than inventing file-level source evidence.
On host timeouts or tool disconnects after possible side-effect calls, inspect process and session state before retrying.

name: code-review-evidence
goal: Review a change for correctness, security, maintainability and scope fit with reproducible findings.
when: Before merging a PR or after a nontrivial code change.
not_when: Pure copy editing with no executable code or system behavior.
steps: Read requirements and diff scope; inspect adjacent source and test context rather than reviewing added lines alone.
Independently test spec compliance, logic, edge cases, concurrency, input trust, secrets and backward compatibility.
Classify each finding by concrete impact and severity; quote precise file/line ranges and a feasible failure scenario.
Validate suspected defects with tests, static analysis or documented language/runtime semantics where possible.
Separate blocking correctness/security issues from optional style and speculative refactors; rank by user impact.
Confirm fixes or record verification gaps and provide a concise merge decision and residual risk.
gate: Every blocking finding has a specific observable failure or contract violation, not an aesthetic preference.
anti: Do not invent line numbers, apply unrelated edits, or claim review coverage beyond examined surfaces.
blocked: If the diff is too large, sample by risk but state unreviewed areas and request decomposition.

name: python-production-engineering
goal: Build and harden Python libraries, services and scientific modules with modern tooling.
when: Developing Python code, packaging, performance work or maintaining Python services.
not_when: The deliverable is not Python and has no Python dependency.
steps: Inspect supported Python versions, environment management, lockfile, import roots, style rules, type checker and packaging boundaries.
Design typed public functions, explicit exceptions, dataclasses/models only where useful, and stable serialization/IO contracts.
Implement using small composable functions and deterministic resource management; avoid mutable defaults and hidden global state.
Cover edge cases with pytest plus property tests when invariants matter; use isolated temporary paths and explicit random seeds.
Run formatting/lint, types, tests, packaging/build and smoke import in the declared environment; benchmark hotspots before optimizing.
Publish reproducible commands, dependency versions, compatibility constraints and observed outcomes.
gate: Imports work on supported versions, tests and declared lint/type gates pass or show exact failures.
anti: Avoid silent bare-except, unpinned fragile dependencies and deceptive performance claims.
blocked: If runtime dependencies or hardware are missing, provide a self-contained test harness and mark integration tests pending.

name: cpp-modern-systems
goal: Implement robust modern C++ components with explicit ownership, numerical and concurrency semantics.
when: Writing or reviewing C++20/23 systems, libraries or performance-critical code.
not_when: No C++ source or ABI is involved.
steps: Identify compiler, standard level, platforms, ABI, allocation model and error-handling policy; map ownership lifetimes before coding.
Design value-based interfaces and strong types for units; use RAII, spans/views with safe lifetimes, const correctness and clear pre/postconditions.
Make concurrent access, cancellation, exceptions and object moves explicit; avoid data races, dangling references and undefined behavior.
Build warnings-as-errors targets and regression tests, including boundary values, overflow, serialization and concurrency interleavings.
Run sanitizers and static checks where supported; use a reproducible microbenchmark and profiles for claimed optimization.
Provide complete headers/source/build configuration, portability notes, measurements and unresolved platform issues.
gate: Declared compilers compile, unit tests pass, sanitizer diagnostics are addressed, and numerical units are coherent.
anti: Never exchange correctness for micro-optimizations before profiling or assume unsafe code is faster.
blocked: For unsupported compilers or architectures, specify precisely what could not be verified.

name: api-contract-engineering
goal: Design evolvable HTTP/RPC/event interfaces with explicit failures and safe compatibility.
when: Introducing or changing endpoints, schemas, SDKs or service contracts.
not_when: Purely internal function with no client contract.
steps: Enumerate consumers, current contract, authentication principal, idempotency needs and data sensitivity.
Define typed request/response/error schemas with version and pagination semantics, edge cases and rate limits.
Choose validation points, authorization, timeout/retry policy, correlation IDs and safe error information boundaries.
Assess compatibility for old clients, API documentation, caching and migration windows before implementing.
Write contract tests, schema checks and negative authorization tests against real handlers or a faithful integration layer.
Deliver examples, generated schemas when applicable, observability events and deprecation plan.
gate: Existing clients remain compatible or have an approved migration; unauthorized calls fail safely.
anti: Never leak internal exceptions, treat authentication as authorization or change response semantics silently.
blocked: When consumer inventory is incomplete, preserve current public behavior and record possible breakages.
special_rules: Do not infer a complete OpenAPI schema from a HAR or captured requests; captured methods, query names, body shapes and status codes are bounded observations.
Mark inferred URL templates and optionality as hypotheses until contract tests or documented server handlers confirm them.

domain_tests.prompt: Use this one-session HAR to draft hypotheses for the API and label any fields whose optionality or authorization behavior is unknown.
domain_tests.expected_behavior: Preserve current workflow scope and avoid assuming REA is needed, installed or authoritative without direct evidence.

name: postgres-schema-rls
goal: Design PostgreSQL schemas, indexes and row-level security from explicit access contracts.
when: Supabase/Postgres data modeling, slow queries, RLS or schema migrations.
not_when: Data is stored in a different engine and Postgres semantics are irrelevant.
steps: Write tenant/user/role access matrix and data invariants before table DDL or RLS policies.
Model keys, constraints, deletion and temporal semantics; check normalization and isolate protected fields.
Design policies for SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE separately and test with least-privilege roles, not only service credentials.
Inspect actual EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) on representative volumes before adding indexes; consider selectivity and write costs.
Develop forward/backward migrations with lock duration, concurrent index creation, backfill checkpoints and rollback constraints.
Run multi-tenant isolation, performance and transactional tests; document grants, policies and index justification.
gate: Cross-tenant access is denied under realistic roles; query tuning cites measured plans.
anti: Do not rely on client-side filters as tenant isolation or use service-role tests to prove RLS.
blocked: If production data distribution is unavailable, label performance estimates provisional.

name: performance-profiling
goal: Optimize a measured application bottleneck while preserving correctness.
when: Slow services, hot functions, high resource usage or performance regressions.
not_when: Premature optimization without a target or observed problem.
steps: Define baseline SLOs, representative load, percentile latency, throughput, memory and cost metrics; fix the test conditions.
Collect profiles, traces and flame graphs to locate time or allocation hotspots instead of guessing from code appearance.
Determine whether constraint is CPU, memory, IO, network, contention, serialization or algorithmic complexity.
Choose one high-impact change and define a before/after hypothesis plus regression or correctness invariant.
Benchmark on the same inputs with warm-up, repetitions and variance; evaluate tail latency and resource shifts.
Deliver measured improvement, changed tradeoffs, reproducibility and monitoring/rollback triggers.
gate: Claimed improvements are statistically/operationally meaningful in comparable runs; behavior remains correct.
anti: Never claim speedups from a single noisy timing or sacrifice safety for throughput.
blocked: If a production-equivalent workload is unavailable, report microbenchmarks as directional only.

name: observability-slo-design
goal: Instrument services for actionable reliability signals and low-noise incident response.
when: Shipping production services or diagnosing poor production visibility.
not_when: Throwaway local scripts with no operations lifecycle.
steps: Identify core user journeys, failure modes, critical dependencies and measurable service-level indicators.
Select latency, error, throughput and saturation signals with clear label cardinality and personally-identifying-data limits.
Propagate trace context, structured events and stable error classification across the request path.
Define SLOs and error budgets based on user impact; alerts should fire on actionable symptoms rather than every implementation event.
Test dashboards with injected or historical failure cases, checking detection delay and false positive behavior.
Write runbooks with owners, triage queries, rollback, communication and post-incident feedback loops.
gate: A controlled failure is detectable and triageable; telemetry excludes secrets and sensitive payloads.
anti: No high-cardinality user identifiers as metric labels or alerts with no response owner.
blocked: If baselines are missing, deploy measurement first before choosing arbitrary target thresholds.
special_rules: Differentiate event instrumentation in a live process, static references to logging, and captured network calls; only actual observations support runtime SLO baselines.
Treat support traces and crash dumps as potentially sensitive evidence requiring access limits.

domain_tests.prompt: My service binary contains a string `request_duration_ms` but no deployed traces. Can that string establish our 99th percentile latency SLO?
domain_tests.expected_behavior: Preserve current workflow scope and avoid assuming REA is needed, installed or authoritative without direct evidence.

name: safe-database-migrations
goal: Plan and execute backward-compatible data changes with reversible checkpoints.
when: Schema evolution, backfills, production migrations or data retention changes.
not_when: Ephemeral development database reset with no preserved data.
steps: Inventory schema consumers, old/new binaries, dataset size, write traffic, locks, ownership and backup/restore capability.
Choose expand-migrate-contract phases and feature flags; avoid simultaneous incompatible code and schema rollouts.
Create idempotent, resumable backfills with bounded batches, monitoring and stop conditions; protect consistency invariants.
Rehearse using production-like data and record actual runtime, locks, transaction logs and failure/restart behavior.
Define checkpoint-based rollout, backward compatibility window, rollback or forward-fix policy and explicit human approvals.
Verify row counts, constraints, checksums, consumer behavior and safe cleanup only after old clients retire.
gate: Old and new versions coexist during the migration window; data invariants and backups are checked.
anti: Never drop columns immediately after a deploy or assume DDL is instant on large tables.
blocked: If rollback cannot restore state, label one-way operations and require explicit approval before execution.

name: ci-release-engineering
goal: Build reproducible CI, supply-chain checks and staged delivery with rollback readiness.
when: Creating or updating CI/CD, packaging, deployment or release automation.
not_when: Pure planning without actual build or release process.
steps: Map source-to-artifact-to-environment path, credentials, deploy permissions, environments and trusted/untrusted triggers.
Create fast deterministic checks first: format, lint, types, unit tests, dependency scan, integration and packaging.
Pin toolchain versions and action dependencies; enforce least-privilege tokens and isolate untrusted pull-request execution.
Build immutable artifacts with provenance, checksums and environment configuration separated from artifact contents.
Rehearse staging rollout, smoke tests, canary thresholds, feature flags and rollback for database/app differences.
Publish release evidence, changelog, monitoring links and on-call ownership with clear failure escalation.
gate: A fresh checkout reproduces artifacts; failing gate blocks release; rollback was rehearsed.
anti: Never run secrets in forked PR contexts or hide failing tests with blanket continue-on-error.
blocked: When access prevents deployment, deliver reviewed config and clearly state it has not been executed.

name: frontend-state-architecture
goal: Design predictable frontend state and component boundaries without excess complexity.
when: A UI has complex shared state, async data or reusable component contracts.
not_when: A small static page with no interactive state.
steps: Map user journeys, persisted versus ephemeral state, server truth, URL state and accessibility behaviors.
Select component boundaries by responsibility; keep primitives composable and avoid boolean prop explosions.
Define loading, error, empty, stale, optimistic, cancellation and race states before wiring APIs.
Make transitions explicit and test them under delayed, reordered and failed network responses.
Check keyboard, screen-reader announcements and focus continuity across async renders and modals.
Validate source-of-truth consistency, memory cleanup, render cost and ease of extension.
gate: No duplicated authoritative state, lost updates or inaccessible transitions in tested journeys.
anti: No premature global stores, nested prop flag matrices or silent optimistic failures.
blocked: If a third-party state library is proposed, justify it against existing project conventions.

name: website-discovery-architecture
goal: Turn a website business goal into a navigable, measurable information architecture.
when: Planning a new site, large redesign, sitemap or navigation model.
not_when: Request is for one self-contained UI element.
steps: Interview available product, audience, conversion and editorial inputs; identify primary jobs-to-be-done, owners and constraints.
Inventory pages, content types, existing analytics, search intents, legal/privacy requirements and content lifecycle.
Define user journeys and a low-depth hierarchy with distinct page responsibilities, canonical URL patterns and contextual navigation.
Create page templates, required fields, breadcrumbs, local search facets and empty/error journeys.
Test proposed labels and findability with task-based tree checks for representative new and returning users.
Ship sitemap, content model, navigation rationale, owner assignments and measurable launch checks.
gate: Top tasks can be located unambiguously; each content type has an owner and canonical destination.
anti: Do not organize only around internal departments or hide important pages behind ambiguous labels.
blocked: Mark assumptions if analytics, users or existing content inventories are unavailable.
special_rules: Browser observation of a live site is optional supporting evidence, not a default prerequisite for a source-backed website design task.
If external app behavior is used as a reference, preserve observable UX criteria without copying its protected art, source or credential-bearing capture.

domain_tests.prompt: Plan a redesign for my owned website using existing source and user interviews; the old browser capture is only optional research.
domain_tests.expected_behavior: Preserve current workflow scope and avoid assuming REA is needed, installed or authoritative without direct evidence.

name: accessible-interface-build
goal: Ship keyboard-operable, semantically correct web interfaces with tested accessible behavior.
when: Building or refactoring interactive web UI, components, forms or navigation.
not_when: Pure graphic mockup with no intended interaction.
steps: Specify semantic structure, expected keyboard sequence, focus transitions, visible state and screen-reader announcements.
Choose native HTML behavior first; use ARIA only to supply missing semantics and avoid conflicting roles.
Implement color contrast, scalable type, reduced-motion handling, touch targets and form validation patterns.
Test keyboard-only journeys, 200%-400% zoom/reflow, errors and asynchronous status changes.
Use accessibility automation to detect common issues then manually test focus order, labels and accessible names.
Produce a component behavior contract and browser evidence for all critical interactions.
gate: Critical flows work without pointer input; automated checks and manual focus tests meet specified WCAG level.
anti: Avoid div-as-button controls, placeholder-only labels or accessibility claims from one scanner.
blocked: If assistive technology tests are unavailable, identify the unverified platforms and test plan.

name: web-performance-core-vitals
goal: Improve real-user web experience by tracing render, network and interaction bottlenecks.
when: Optimizing loading, INP, LCP, CLS, bundle weight or caching.
not_when: No observed web performance issue and no target measurement.
steps: Choose representative routes, device/network conditions and existing field-versus-lab baselines; identify percentile targets.
Capture navigation traces, resource waterfall, main-thread long tasks, layout shifts and hydration costs.
Attribute poor metrics to specific script, CSS, media, fonts, server response or event handlers.
Apply scoped interventions: caching, right-sized media, scheduling, code splitting, preloading or layout reservation.
Rerun matched before/after tests and check visual/functional regressions, including cold-cache and adverse-network paths.
Deliver metrics with measurement method, residual bottlenecks, expected field impact and rollback triggers.
gate: Comparable measurements improve the targeted metric without breaking user flows or accessibility.
anti: Do not optimize only Lighthouse scores while ignoring real users or misattribute lab variance.
blocked: When field telemetry is missing, label laboratory outcomes as estimates.

name: responsive-design-system
goal: Create a reusable responsive component system with predictable tokens and states.
when: Multiple pages or products need coherent responsive components and patterns.
not_when: One-off graphic or single nonreusable visual.
steps: Audit existing design primitives, variants, content density, localization and user device distribution.
Define semantic color, typography, spacing, elevation, breakpoints and motion tokens with contrast and theme rules.
Build a small composable component inventory with explicit props, error/loading/disabled states and accessible semantics.
Model responsive behavior by content priority and container constraints rather than device names alone.
Document examples, usage/non-usage criteria, migration notes and visual regression fixtures.
Validate long copy, RTL where relevant, zoom, dark mode, touch and keyboard controls on representative screens.
gate: Variants are composable, accessible and consistent across the supported viewport matrix.
anti: Avoid hundreds of one-off tokens, breakpoint patchwork and prop combinations that create invalid states.
blocked: If the brand system is undefined, propose token defaults as provisional.

name: browser-qa-cross-device
goal: Evaluate browser behavior through reproducible end-to-end tests and visual regression evidence.
when: Web app release QA, flaky UI, responsive regressions or browser-specific failures.
not_when: Only unit-level business logic changes with no browser behavior.
steps: Derive risk-based critical routes, devices, browsers, locales and assistive input modes from product analytics and support reports.
Write deterministic test scenarios with seeded data, isolated users, stable selectors and explicit network/time assumptions.
Test happy paths, errors, slow requests, offline/reconnect, back navigation, multi-tab and permissions where relevant.
Capture screenshots, trace files, console errors and network requests on failed tests; triage environment versus product defects.
Run responsive visual comparisons with explicit approved baselines and documented tolerances.
Publish a browser matrix, reproducible issues with artifacts and an evidence-backed go/no-go recommendation.
gate: All critical journeys passed on required browsers; known defects have impact and owners.
anti: Avoid arbitrary sleeps, screenshot-only testing and silently updating failing baselines.
blocked: Report unsupported browser/device coverage rather than implying it was exercised.
special_rules: If comparing runtime behavior across releases, record exact build/capture identities, deterministic seed state, service-worker policy and response-body capture coverage.
Separate screenshots or DOM appearance from proof of server persistence; verify state with permitted independent reads.

domain_tests.prompt: I have two screenshots from browsers and want to assert an order is persisted on the server. Explain what independent check the test still needs.
domain_tests.expected_behavior: Preserve current workflow scope and avoid assuming REA is needed, installed or authoritative without direct evidence.
